evals.prompt: Show me how to set up the Directus SDK with TypeScript types and do basic CRUD
expectations: Uses createDirectus with composable pattern (rest, staticToken)
Shows TypeScript interface for schema
Shows readItems with fields and filter
Shows createItem example
Shows updateItem example
Uses correct imports from @directus/sdk

evals.prompt: How do I subscribe to real-time changes on a collection with the Directus SDK?
evals.expected_output: realtime() composable, connect(), subscribe(), for-await loop
expectations: Uses realtime() composable in client setup
Calls client.connect() before subscribing
Uses client.subscribe() with collection name and event type
Shows for-await-of loop for consuming events
Includes correct imports (createDirectus, realtime, staticToken)

evals.prompt: How do I log in with email and password using the Directus SDK in a Node.js script?
evals.expected_output: authentication('json') client, login with a payload object, stopRefreshing for one-shot scripts
expectations: Calls client.login with a single payload object { email, password }, not two positional arguments
Uses authentication('json') for Node.js because the default cookie mode needs a cookie jar
Mentions optional login options (otp, mode, provider) and the LDAP identifier payload
Reads credentials from environment variables
Mentions Node 22 or later for SDK 26 and stopRefreshing for one-shot scripts

evals.prompt: I use the Directus SDK in a Next.js Server Component and wrote createDirectus(url).with(rest({ cache: 'no-store' })) but TypeScript complains. How do I control caching?
evals.expected_output: rest() has no cache option; pass fetch options through onRequest or withOptions
expectations: Explains that RestConfig has no cache option (TS2353) and that credentials, onRequest and onResponse are the only options
Shows rest({ onRequest }) for every request or withOptions(command, options) for one command to pass cache or next.tags to fetch
Says a readItems command should be built inside the request call (not stored in a const) so the collection name type-checks
Does not suggest putting the access token in a URL

evals.prompt: My Next.js health check does directus.request(readItems('directus_collections')) and fails. What should I call instead?
evals.expected_output: System collections use typed commands; readItems refuses directus_* collections
expectations: Says readItems on a directus_* collection is a type error and throws 'Cannot use readItems for core collections' at runtime
Recommends readCollections() for collections and serverPing() for a connection check
Lists readMe, readUsers, readRoles, readPolicies or readFiles as the typed commands for other system collections
